To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CMTI-I is a zinc-binding protein; its zinc coordination geometry is tetrahedral and the zinc ion is coordinated by four glutamate/glutamine side chains; CMTI-I crystallized in a complex with zinc is structurally very similar to the enzyme-inhibitory complex; and CMTI-I has an unusual conformation for Ala18 that is due to geometrical strain caused by the disulfide bridges.

CMTI-I crystallizes as a 4Zn complex with the metal ions coordinated in a symmetric fashion by glutamate and glutamic acid side-chain carboxylate groups and that the structure of the inhibitor in the zinc complex is very similar to its structure in the trypsin complex.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of the squash trypsin inhibitors (CMTI-I and CMTI-II) and their complexes with trypsin and trypsin-like enzymes.
the structure of a protein complexed with zinc and the role of the metal.
the structural basis of protein stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure of the squash trypsin-inhibitor-zinc complex is a very interesting one, and the structure determination is an example of a successful application of direct methods in the presence of a special position.
the stereochemistry of the present protein structure is consistent with the X-ray diffraction data and that the structure has been solved in an unbiased manner.

the structure of CMTI-I is very similar to the structure of CMB-I in complex with bovine trypsin, with the exception of the Met8Leul mutation, the higher mobility loop around residue 24 and a higher solvent content in the crystal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of CMTI-I is not a simple protein fold but is rather a highly constrained one, with a very compact core and a high degree of internal order.
the crystal structure of CMTI-I is a good model for a trypsin inhibitor and that the metal coordination is not a result of the crystallization procedure.
the present structure of CMTI-I is the first example of a protein that has been crystallized in a metal complex and whose structure was solved without any prior knowledge of the metal position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of CMTI-I is not significantly affected by the substitution of a methionine by a leucine residue.
the structure of a metal complex of a small protein, in this case squash trypsin-inhibitor, can be determined at atomic resolution by using direct methods in the presence of the metal.
the structure determination of the present protein variant has provided a new example of a protein fold with a tetrahedral metal coordination site.
